title: E_A molecular-identity measurement architecture
abstract: This synthetic measurement program asks whether the proposed early intermediate can be identified on the same recovered molecule before any mechanistic conclusion is made, without treating the measurement object as a competing biological hypothesis.
disposition_reason: It is retained to resolve identifiability before causal attribution, not as a biological finalist.
nearest_prior_art: Generic molecular-identity and provenance measurements applied outside this synthetic decision context.
strongest_reason: It can prevent causal interpretation when the required molecular object is not identifiable.
weakest_causal_edge: Recovery bias may still decouple the observed molecule from the productive intermediate.
pairwise_summary: Kept outside biological ranking because it is a measurement architecture.
reviewer_disagreement: Reviewers differed on technical recovery feasibility.
reviewer_critiques: Target linkage, provenance, sequence, and length class must be resolved on the same molecule.
reentry_condition: Promote to an implementation plan only after recovery bias and same-molecule linkage are bounded.
scientific_summary: The E_A object is a measurement architecture for identifying a proposed early intermediate before assigning mechanism.
causal_mechanism: It does not posit a new biological mechanism; it conditions downstream inference on molecular identity and provenance.
evidence_basis: Synthetic measurement logic and general identifiability principles.
next_discriminating_experiment: Demonstrate same-molecule target linkage, provenance, sequence, length class, and quantified recovery bias.
